This page covers O*NET 11-3031.03. Investment fund managers organize research, portfolio decisions, risk monitoring and record handoffs within a fund’s objectives and mandate. U.S. wage and employment figures refer to the broader Financial Managers occupation 11-3031.

entries: Objects of work | Fund assets and investment objectives, investment authorization and limits, research and valuation materials, trade and execution channels, and disclosure and compliance requirements; investment management within fiduciary and compliance boundaries.

Checkable outputs | Reviewable investment decisions and their basis, portfolio and risk limit records, trade and execution records, valuation and pricing records, and performance and compliance disclosure materials; results must be traceable to authorization, data sources and policy versions.

Complete workflow | Confirm authorization and investment objectives → research and valuation → develop and execute strategies → monitor trades and execution → review performance and risks → compliance disclosure and regulatory responses.

paragraphs: Key judgments | O*NET work context shows: email daily 100%; telephone conversations daily 92%; workweeks exceeding 40 hours 87%; face-to-face discussions daily 83%; considerable freedom in decision-making 63%; decisions daily 66%; extremely competitive 61%. Judgments depend on authorization and limits, research and valuation evidence, and compliance requirements for conflicts of interest and disclosure.

Environment and pace | Work primarily involves desk-based analysis, trading hours and communication: indoor controlled environment daily 87%; sitting continually or almost continually 75%; constant contact with others 51%; exactness or accuracy extremely important 44%; time pressure daily 40%; extremely serious consequences of error 32%; very high responsibility for others' work outcomes 40%; coordinating or leading others very important 32%. The pace is driven by market hours and performance cycles.
O*NET 11-3031.03 describes this occupation’s tasks and work context. U.S. wages come from OEWS and projections from BLS Table 1.2.

First verify this job's objects (fund assets and investment objectives, authorization and limits, research and valuation materials), inputs (investment authorization and limits, market and financial data sources, valuation and pricing policies, disclosure and compliance requirements), and deliverables (investment decisions and their basis, portfolio and risk limit records, trade and valuation records, performance and disclosure materials). Treat anything unverified as pending verification; market sentiment or proxy scopes cannot replace authorization, valuation conventions and disclosure requirements.

Assess the complete workflow through four steps: verify inputs (confirm authorization and limits, data sources and policy versions) → limit tasks (decide and execute only within authorization and compliance scope) → execute and document (complete research, trades, valuation and record trails to standards) → review and escalate (stop immediately and report limit breaches, valuation disputes, conflicts of interest or disclosure issues). A complete workflow requires verifiable authorization, data and policies, rather than looking only at performance.

They cannot be interchanged solely by job title; the scope should not extend to other adjacent occupations or use proxies to replace institutional authorization, fiduciary duties and ultimate responsibility.

Objects of work and AI boundaries for investment fund managers: which steps may receive assistance and which judgments must remain human responsibilities.

Direct answer | Based on investment research, valuation, trading and disclosure tasks, the editorial suggestion is to first trial assistance with data organization, scenario calculations and summary drafts using fictional materials. Generative AI risks involving errors, privacy and information integrity require review under the NIST framework; this is not an empirical finding of efficiency gains or adoption rates in this occupation. Fund decisions still follow specific institutional authorization; this page provides no replacement probability or timeline.

Evidence explanation | O*NET supports investment fund managers' tasks, work context and preparation information; it cannot establish widespread AI adoption. NIST AI 600-1 provides cross-domain generative AI risk categories, not employment outcomes for this occupation; the FSB public summary of IOSCO 2021 regulatory measures discusses asset managers' supervision, testing and data quality, not the proportion adopting generative AI. The following trials and control points are FermatMind editorial synthesis.

Differences | The editorial suggestion is to trial easily reviewed record organization, calculations and text drafts separately from authorized decisions. Various tasks may receive assistance, but actual time savings, accuracy and institutional adoption require separate measurement; they cannot be inferred directly from hot technology lists or task descriptions.

Responsibility chain | From confirming authorization and limits, model and tool processing, human review, decision and disclosure approval to record trails, every step must identify who is responsible and retain traceable evidence; fiduciary decisions and disclosure must not rely solely on a model.

Turning point | First define permitted input data, verification responsibilities and stop conditions, then trial research and document assistance. Only after comparison with a human baseline and documentation of errors can a tool's usefulness for that task be assessed; this does not predict efficiency gains or job changes in this occupation.

Potential assistance: organizing market and financial data, factor and scenario analysis, research summaries, and report and compliance document drafts. These outputs can be checked afterward, but original data, authorization and policy versions must still be revisited.

Human control points: revisit original data and authorization records, review key judgments, and take responsibility for authorization and limits, valuation determinations, execution decisions and disclosure.

For investment fund managers, which interests, abilities and working styles matter more? This page discusses fit only through work samples and responsibility boundaries, without using personality labels to replace judgments of qualifications and performance.

Direct answer | Fit signals are handling investment decisions under authorization and policies, maintaining discipline under intensity and competition, accurately documenting evidence and assumptions, and escalating uncertainty or limit breaches, rather than personality labels. Interest and personality tools can only help design trials; they cannot determine hiring eligibility, authorization or performance.

Positive signals | Completing research and valuation, portfolio and limit management, and trade and execution records under procedures; checking authorization and policy versions and identifying conflicts of interest and disclosure issues; leaving reviewable process records and handing over accurately within fiduciary boundaries.

Caution conditions | Risk signals include operating beyond authorization or limits, continuing despite inconsistent valuation and pricing conventions, failing to disclose conflicts of interest, noncompliant marketing materials, and replacing fiduciary judgment with model output. If intense decision responsibility, long working hours and competitive pressure are difficult for you, treat them as practical costs that require careful consideration.
Use Sheet F to check the reporting period and review status, retain conflicting values and name the reviewer for each discrepancy.

Conclusion | Activity preferences are closer to a combination of organizational initiative, following procedures and research inquiry (O*NET interest code ECI); interest codes can only help design trials and cannot determine hiring eligibility or performance.

Conclusion | This page does not predict investment fund manager performance from a single personality label; assess through work samples involving research, limit checks, communication and record trails. Personality and cognitive measurements must be checked separately from hiring, qualifications and authorization.

Conclusion | RIASEC or personality frameworks can only help raise questions; they cannot replace evidence of work samples, learning ability, qualifications and actual performance for this occupation. No tool conclusion constitutes a hiring, authorization or appointment judgment.
A proposed action exceeds investment authority, a risk limit or product scope, or the applicable limit cannot be confirmed.

Valuation and pricing risks | Trigger: inconsistent valuation methods, model assumptions or pricing sources, or failure to follow policies. Consequence: possible distortion of net asset values and performance. Controls: follow valuation policies, retain assumptions and sources, and conduct regular independent reviews. Boundary: valuation disputes follow valuation committee procedures and policies.
A related-party or personal transaction or another outside interest creates an unresolved conflict.

Disclosure and marketing compliance risks | Trigger: noncompliant or misleading offering documents, performance displays or marketing materials. Consequence: possible regulatory penalties and investor losses. Controls: review materials under disclosure and marketing standards, and retain review and version records. Boundary: disclosure content follows regulatory requirements and policies.

Common escalation rule | If authorization, valuation or disclosure conditions are insufficient, first stop the relevant step and hand over facts, impacts and pending questions in reviewable records to the authorized person responsible. Do not bypass regulatory requirements, fiduciary duties or institutional authorization, or substitute model output for investment and disclosure decisions.

For public securities investment funds in mainland China, portfolio managers provide investment rationale and report materials within their role. The fund management entity prepares and publishes the periodic report, its board and directors vouch for its contents, and the custodian reviews specified material including the portfolio report and issues an opinion. Qualification boundaries | Courses, certificates or examinations do not automatically grant investment authorization, fiduciary decision or external disclosure authority. Education, certificates, qualification certification, hiring, institutional authorization and fiduciary authority are distinct statuses; specific requirements depend on jurisdiction and institution.

Start with supervised research and records. With the relevant authority, a manager can make portfolio decisions, monitor limits and hand over reporting materials. Formal filing and public disclosure follow the process of the responsible entity.

career_risk_cards.direct_answer: Risks must be addressed through triggers, consequences, controls and escalation boundaries.
career_risk_cards.evidence_scope: Risk scenarios are editorial analysis based on occupational tasks; sources support the task context, not accident rates or statutory permissions. Specific qualifications and authorization must be checked against local rules.
career_risk_cards.heading: Work risks and boundaries for investment fund managers

risks.consequence: May cause breaches of fiduciary obligations and major losses.
risks.mitigation: If a limit is breached or authority is unclear, pause the affected action, retain source data, the relevant limit and the action record, and escalate to risk or compliance. Internal exceptions apply only where policy permits them. Legal, fund-contract and product constraints still apply.
risks.title: Authorization and limits

risks.consequence: May distort net asset values and performance.
risks.mitigation: Follow valuation policies, retain assumptions and sources, and conduct regular independent reviews.
risks.title: Valuation and pricing

risks.consequence: May cause compliance risks and fiduciary issues.
risks.mitigation: Pause affected decisions when a conflict is unresolved. Declare it, recuse or refer it to compliance under policy, and keep the record. Applicable law, fund-contract terms and product constraints remain binding.
risks.title: Conflicts of interest

risks.consequence: May cause regulatory penalties and investor losses.
risks.mitigation: Verify the version and review status of reporting materials. Pause the handoff and escalate material omissions or discrepancies. The responsible entity handles required disclosure under its applicable process.
risks.title: Disclosure and marketing

risks.consequence: May cause internal control failures and compliance risks.
risks.mitigation: Complete review and record trails under policies; do not substitute performance targets for procedures.
risks.title: Internal controls and review

risks.consequence: May bypass regulatory requirements, fiduciary duties or institutional authorization.
risks.mitigation: First stop the relevant step and hand over facts, impacts and pending questions to the authorized person responsible.
risks.scenario: Continuing despite insufficient authorization, valuation or disclosure conditions.
risks.title: Authorization and record risks
